intro: You are now at the Alâeddin Mosque in Konya, a mosque and complex in Konya province, built over 1155–1221. This was the congregational mosque of the Anatolian Seljuk capital: a flat-roofed hall on forty-two reused columns, with the tombs of eight sultans beside it.
history: The mosque stands on the mound at the centre of Konya, beside what was once the Seljuk palace. Building began in 1155 and finished only in 1221, under Alâeddin Keykubad I — which is why its parts follow different plans. Look up: forty-two reused columns carry a flat wooden ceiling. And in its courtyard, two tombs hold eight Seljuk sultans.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the wooden-ceilinged hall, the reused columns, the ebony minbar and the sultans' tombs.
facts: Did you know? The ebony minbar of 1155 is the earliest dated piece of Anatolian Seljuk woodwork, and it was built entirely with interlocking joints, without a single nail. Eight Seljuk sultans lie buried in the two tombs in its courtyard.
outro: This brings our tour of the Alâeddin Mosque in Konya to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
